```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
```

modelcompR is a native R port of
[ModelingToolkit.jl](https://github.com/SciML/ModelingToolkit.jl). A model
is a set of symbolic equations; `mtkcompile()` simplifies it and generates the
R functions that the numerical solvers call. This article walks through the
basic workflow: declare variables, write equations, compile, build a
problem, solve and inspect the solution.

```{r setup}
library(modelcompR)
```

## A first order lag

The time variable and its derivative operator come with the package.
`t_nounits` is used instead of `t`, which would mask `base::t()`.

```{r}
t <- t_nounits
D <- D_nounits
variables("x(t)")
parameters("tau")
```

`variables()` and `parameters()` mirror `@variables` and `@parameters`:
they create the symbols and assign them in the calling environment.
Equations are R formulas, so they read as in Julia.

```{r}
sys <- System(list(D(x) ~ (1 - x) / tau), t, name = "lag")
sys <- mtkcompile(sys)
unknowns(sys)
```

A problem takes the values of the unknowns and the parameters as equations,
and the time span.

```{r}
prob <- ODEProblem(sys, list(x ~ 0, tau ~ 3), c(0, 10))
sol <- solve(prob)
sol$retcode
```

The solution is indexed by symbols or by any expression of the model, and is
called as a function for dense output.

```{r}
head(sol[x])
sol(5)
head(sol[(1 - x) / tau])
plot(sol)
```

## A second order equation

Higher derivatives are lowered to first order systems, as in ModelingToolkit,
and equations that only define a variable become observed equations.

```{r}
variables("y(t)", "v(t)")
parameters("k = 2")
osc <- mtkcompile(System(list(D(D(y)) ~ -k * y, v ~ 2 * D(y)), t, name = "osc"))
unknowns(osc)
observed(osc)
sol <- solve(ODEProblem(osc, list(y ~ 1, D(y) ~ 0), c(0, 5)))
sol(c(1, 2, 3), idxs = v)
```

## Choosing a solver

`solve()` picks a method automatically. Any of the ported OrdinaryDiffEq
methods can be named instead, with the usual tolerances.

```{r}
sol_tsit <- solve(prob, Tsit5(), reltol = 1e-10, abstol = 1e-10)
sol_rodas <- solve(prob, Rodas5P())
c(sol_tsit(10)[1], sol_rodas(10)[1], 1 - exp(-10 / 3))
```
